card.name: Auxiliary verbs before reported findings
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as have, been, which, in, has right after a subject and before a verb like reported, shown or occurred. Mostly in warnings about cases or trial findings, plus a few 'Did you find this article useful' prompts.

modes.label: Have/been before reports
modes.description: Helper verbs or linking words leading into 'reported', 'shown' or 'occurred' in adverse event and warning text.
modes.example: Cases of intracranial hypertension (IH) have<< been>> reported in the postmarketing setting

modes.label: Article feedback prompt
modes.description: Words in 'Did you find this article useful/helpful?' website prompts.
modes.example: Did<< you>> find this article helpful? Yes No

card.writes: It pushes toward connective phrasing that continues a general statement (Chinese words like 'but if', 'tend to', 'they will'), and away from past-tense completed-event verbs.
card.plain: It fires on small helper words in sentences like 'cases have been reported' that lead into a finding.
